ESV.1: Sarah lived 127 years; these were the years of the life of Sarah.
ESV.2: And Sarah died at Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan, and Abraham went in to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.
ESV.3: And Abraham rose up from before his dead and said to the Hittites,
ESV.4: “I am a sojourner and foreigner among you; give me property among you for a burying place, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.”
ESV.6: “Hear us, my lord; you are a prince of God  among us. Bury your dead in the choicest of our tombs. None of us will withhold from you his tomb to hinder you from burying your dead.”
ESV.7: Abraham rose and bowed to the Hittites, the people of the land.
ESV.8: And he said to them, “If you are willing that I should bury my dead out of my sight, hear me and entreat for me Ephron the son of Zohar,
ESV.9: that he may give me the cave of Machpelah, which he owns; it is at the end of his field. For the full price let him give it to me in your presence as property for a burying place.”
ESV.10: Now Ephron was sitting among the Hittites, and Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the hearing of the Hittites, of all who went in at the gate of his city,
ESV.11: “No, my lord, hear me: I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it. In the sight of the sons of my people I give it to you. Bury your dead.”
ESV.12: Then Abraham bowed down before the people of the land.
ESV.13: And he said to Ephron in the hearing of the people of the land, “But if you will, hear me: I give the price of the field. Accept it from me, that I may bury my dead there.”
ESV.15: “My lord, listen to me: a piece of land worth four hundred shekels  of silver, what is that between you and me? Bury your dead.”
ESV.16: Abraham listened to Ephron, and Abraham weighed out for Ephron the silver that he had named in the hearing of the Hittites, four hundred shekels of silver, according to the weights current among the merchants.
ESV.17: So the field of Ephron in Machpelah, which was to the east of Mamre, the field with the cave that was in it and all the trees that were in the field, throughout its whole area, was made over
ESV.18: to Abraham as a possession in the presence of the Hittites, before all who went in at the gate of his city.
ESV.19: After this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah east of Mamre (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan.
ESV.20: The field and the cave that is in it were made over to Abraham as property for a burying place by the Hittites.

NASB.1: Now Sarah lived one hundred and twenty-seven years; [these were] the years of the life of Sarah.

NASB.7: So Abraham rose and bowed to the people of the land, the sons of Heth.
NASB.8: And he spoke with them, saying, 'If it is your wish [for me] to bury my dead out of my sight, hear me, and approach Ephron the son of Zohar for me,

NLT.2: she died at Kiriath-arba (now called Hebron) in the land of Canaan. There Abraham mourned and wept for her.
NLT.3: Then, leaving her body, he said to the Hittite elders,
NLT.4: “Here I am, a stranger and a foreigner among you. Please sell me a piece of land so I can give my wife a proper burial.”
NLT.6: “Listen, my lord, you are an honored prince among us. Choose the finest of our tombs and bury her there. No one here will refuse to help you in this way.”
NLT.7: Then Abraham bowed low before the Hittites
NLT.8: and said, “Since you are willing to help me in this way, be so kind as to ask Ephron son of Zohar
NLT.9: to let me buy his cave at Machpelah, down at the end of his field. I will pay the full price in the presence of witnesses, so I will have a permanent burial place for my family.”
NLT.10: Ephron was sitting there among the others, and he answered Abraham as the others listened, speaking publicly before all the Hittite elders of the town.
NLT.11: “No, my lord,” he said to Abraham, “please listen to me. I will give you the field and the cave. Here in the presence of my people, I give it to you. Go and bury your dead.”
NLT.12: Abraham again bowed low before the citizens of the land,
NLT.13: and he replied to Ephron as everyone listened. “No, listen to me. I will buy it from you. Let me pay the full price for the field so I can bury my dead there.”
NLT.15: “My lord, please listen to me. The land is worth 400 pieces of silver, but what is that between friends? Go ahead and bury your dead.”
NLT.16: So Abraham agreed to Ephron’s price and paid the amount he had suggested — 400 pieces of silver, weighed according to the market standard. The Hittite elders witnessed the transaction.
NLT.17: So Abraham bought the plot of land belonging to Ephron at Machpelah, near Mamre. This included the field itself, the cave that was in it, and all the surrounding trees.
NLT.18: It was transferred to Abraham as his permanent possession in the presence of the Hittite elders at the city gate.
NLT.19: Then Abraham buried his wife, Sarah, there in Canaan, in the cave of Machpelah, near Mamre (also called Hebron).
NLT.20: So the field and the cave were transferred from the Hittites to Abraham for use as a permanent burial place.

CSB17.1: Now Sarah lived 127 years; these were all the years of her life.
CSB17.2: Sarah died in Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron <sup>ⓕ</sup>) in the land of Canaan, and Abraham went to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.
CSB17.3: Then Abraham got up from beside his dead wife and spoke to the Hethites:
CSB17.4: “I am an alien residing among you. <sup>ⓖ</sup> Give me burial property among you so that I can bury my dead.” <sup>[1]</sup> <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.6: “Listen to us, my lord. You are a prince of God <sup>[3]</sup> among us. Bury your dead in our finest burial place. <sup>[4]</sup> None of us will withhold from you his burial place for burying your dead.”
CSB17.7: Then Abraham rose and bowed down to the Hethites, the people of the land.
CSB17.8: He said to them, “If you are willing for me to bury my dead, listen to me and ask Ephron son of Zohar on my behalf
CSB17.9: to give me the cave of Machpelah that belongs to him; it is at the end of his field. Let him give it to me in your presence, for the full price, as burial property.”
CSB17.10: Ephron was sitting among the Hethites. So in the hearing <sup>[5]</sup> of all the Hethites who came to the gate of his city, <sup>ⓘ</sup> Ephron the Hethite answered Abraham:
CSB17.11: “No, my lord. Listen to me. I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it. I give it to you in the sight <sup>[6]</sup> of my people. Bury your dead.”
CSB17.12: Abraham bowed down to the people of the land
CSB17.13: and said to Ephron in the hearing of the people of the land, “Listen to me, if you please. Let me pay the price of the field. Accept it from me, and let me bury my dead there.”
CSB17.14: Ephron answered Abraham and said to him,
CSB17.15: “My lord, listen to me. Land worth four hundred shekels of silver <sup>ⓙ</sup>  — what is that between you and me? Bury your dead.”
CSB17.16: Abraham agreed with Ephron, and Abraham weighed out to Ephron the silver that he had agreed to in the hearing of the Hethites: four hundred standard shekels <sup>[7]</sup> of silver. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.17: So Ephron’s field <sup>ⓛ</sup> at Machpelah near Mamre — the field with its cave and all the trees anywhere within the boundaries of the field — became
CSB17.18: Abraham’s possession in the sight of all the Hethites who came to the gate of his city.
CSB17.19: After this, Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field at Machpelah near Mamre (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan.
CSB17.20: The field with its cave passed from the Hethites to Abraham <sup>ⓜ</sup> as burial property.

AMP.1: Sarah lived a hundred and twenty-seven years; this was the length of the life of Sarah.
AMP.2: Sarah died in Kiriath-arba(that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan, and Abraham went to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.
AMP.3: Then Abraham stood up before his dead [wife's body], and spoke to the sons of Heth (Hittites), saying,
AMP.4: "I am a stranger and a sojourner (resident alien) among you; give (sell) me property for a burial place among you so that I may bury my dead [in the proper manner]."
AMP.6: "Listen to us, my lord; you are a prince of God [a mighty prince] among us; bury your dead in the choicest of our graves; none of us will refuse you his grave or hinder you from burying your dead [wife]."
AMP.7: So Abraham stood up and bowed to the people of the land, the Hittites.
AMP.8: And Abraham said to them, "If you are willing to grant my dead a [proper] burial, listen to me, and plead with Ephron the son of Zohar for me,
AMP.9: so that he may give (sell) me the cave of Machpelah which he owns—it is at the end of his field; let him give it to me here in your presence for the full price as a burial site [which I may keep forever among you]."
AMP.10: Now Ephron was present there among the sons of Heth; so within the hearing of all the sons of Heth and all who were entering the gate of his city, Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham, saying,
AMP.11: "No, my lord, hear me; I give you the [entire] field, and I also give you the cave that is in it. In the presence of the men of my people I give (sell) it to you; bury your dead [there]."
AMP.12: Then Abraham bowed down before the people of the land.
AMP.13: He said to Ephron in the presence of the people of the land, "If you will only please listen to me and accept my offer. I will give you the price of the field; accept it from me and I will bury my dead there."
AMP.15: "My lord, listen to me. The land [you seek] is worth four hundred shekels of silver; what is that between you and me? So bury your dead."
AMP.16: So Abraham listened to Ephron [and agreed to his terms]; and he weighed out for Ephron the [amount of] silver which he had named in the hearing of the Hittites: four hundred shekels of silver, according to the weights current among the merchants.
AMP.17: So the field of Ephron in Machpelah, which was to the east of Mamre (Hebron)—the field and the cave which was in it, and all the trees that were in the field and in all its borders around it—were deeded over [legally]
AMP.18: to Abraham as his possession in the presence of the Hittites, before all who were entering at the gate of his city.
AMP.19: After this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah to the east of Mamre (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan.
AMP.20: The field and the cave in it were deeded over to Abraham by the Hittites as a [permanent] possession and burial place.

MSG.2: Sarah died in Kiriath Arba, present-day Hebron, in the land of Canaan. Abraham mourned for Sarah and wept.
MSG.3: Then Abraham got up from mourning his dead wife and spoke to the Hittites:
MSG.4: "I know I'm only an outsider here among you, but sell me a burial plot so that I can bury my dead decently."
MSG.6: "Why, you're no mere outsider here with us, you're a prince of God! Bury your dead wife in the best of our burial sites. None of us will refuse you a place for burial."
MSG.7: Then Abraham got up, bowed respectfully to the people of the land, the Hittites,
MSG.8: and said, "If you're serious about helping me give my wife a proper burial, intercede for me with Ephron son of Zohar.
